extracted.name: Vanilla Genoise (Sponge Cake)
extracted.description: This is a recipe from a wonderful book about bakery by the Argentine chef pâtissier Osvaldo Gross. It’s the basic cake I use for any birthday cake. A Genoise (or génoise) is a classic Italian and French sponge cake named after the city of Genoa. Unlike traditional sponge cakes that use chemical leaveners like baking powder, a true Genoise relies entirely on air whipped into whole eggs and sugar to provide volume. It has a light, elastic, and somewhat dry texture, making it an ideal, sturdy base for absorbing flavored syrups, liqueurs, and supporting heavy fillings like buttercream, pastry cream, or fruit.
instruction_lines: For the cake: Place the eggs and sugar on top of a double boiler. Beat until you reach 40°C (it feels hot when touched with your fingers). In the photos I am making two genoises, therefore doubling the ingredients.
Remove from heat, transfer to an electric mixer and, at medium high speed, whisk to a ribbon (10-12 minutes). Add vanilla.
Sift the flour twice. Add it gradually to the eggs, mixing with a spatula in a soft and enveloping way.
Butter and flour a 24-cm round and 4-cm high mold. Pour into the mold and bake at 180°C (355°F) for 30 to 35 minutes.
The genoise is ready when it begins to retract at the edges and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out dry. Remove from the oven and let stand for 5 minutes. Invert on a grid and unmold.
To store in the refrigerator, let cool completely, wrap in film and store up to 1 week. Decorate once it is cool.
